Okay, so I'm trying to figure out the positive effect of using robots in car assembly. The options are A to D. I remember that robots are used in factories, so maybe they make things faster. I think when robots do the work, humans don't have to, which might mean fewer people are needed. But wait, the question is about a positive effect, so maybe it's not about fewer jobs. Instead, it could be that robots work faster or more accurately.

Option A says the assembly takes more time. That doesn't make sense because robots are supposed to be efficient. So A is probably wrong. Option B says more workers are needed. That doesn't sound right either because robots replace workers, not require more. So B is likely incorrect.

Option C mentions fewer injuries to workers. I've heard that in factories, manual labor can be dangerous, so robots might reduce accidents. That could be a positive effect. Option D says more mistakes are made. I don't think so; robots are precise, so they probably make fewer mistakes than humans. So D is probably wrong.

Putting it all together, the positive effect is likely C: There are fewer injuries to workers. That makes the most sense because robots handle the repetitive and potentially hazardous tasks.
